title: Above Average Salary
statement:
Find the employees who are paid more than the company average.

The `employees` table has one row per employee:

- `id`: the employee's id
- `name`: their full name, unique
- `department`: the department they work in
- `salary`: their yearly salary in dollars

Return two columns, `name` and `salary`, for every employee whose salary is greater than the average salary of all employees. An employee paid exactly the average is not included. Order the rows by `salary` from highest to lowest, then by `name` alphabetically.

Expected output:

```text
     name     | salary
--------------+--------
 Chloe Martin | 112000
 Ana Torres   |  98000
 Grace Kim    |  98000
(3 rows)
```
setup:
CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  department TEXT NOT NULL,
  salary INTEGER NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO employees (id, name, department, salary) VALUES
  (1, 'Ana Torres', 'Engineering', 98000),
  (2, 'Ben Okafor', 'Sales', 61000),
  (3, 'Chloe Martin', 'Engineering', 112000),
  (4, 'Dev Patel', 'Support', 48000),
  (5, 'Emma Larsen', 'Marketing', 72000),
  (6, 'Felix Wagner', 'Sales', 67000),
  (7, 'Grace Kim', 'Engineering', 98000),
  (8, 'Hiro Tanaka', 'Support', 52000);

tests.output:
name     | salary
--------------+--------
 Chloe Martin | 112000
 Ana Torres   |  98000
 Grace Kim    |  98000
(3 rows)

tests.stdin: INSERT INTO employees (id, name, department, salary) VALUES (9, 'Iris Novak', 'Engineering', 190000);
tests.output:
name     | salary
--------------+--------
 Iris Novak   | 190000
 Chloe Martin | 112000
 Ana Torres   |  98000
 Grace Kim    |  98000
(4 rows)

tests.stdin:
UPDATE employees SET salary = 80000 WHERE name = 'Ben Okafor';
UPDATE employees SET salary = 50000 WHERE name = 'Grace Kim';
tests.output:
name     | salary
--------------+--------
 Chloe Martin | 112000
 Ana Torres   |  98000
 Ben Okafor   |  80000
(3 rows)

name     | salary
--------------+--------
 Emma Larsen  |  72000
 Felix Wagner |  67000
 Ben Okafor   |  61000
(3 rows)

tests.stdin:
UPDATE employees SET salary = 84000 WHERE name = 'Dev Patel';
INSERT INTO employees (id, name, department, salary) VALUES (9, 'Iris Novak', 'Marketing', 80500);
tests.output:
name     | salary
--------------+--------
 Chloe Martin | 112000
 Ana Torres   |  98000
 Grace Kim    |  98000
 Dev Patel    |  84000
(4 rows)

hints: A subquery in parentheses that returns a single value can stand anywhere a number can, for example on the right of `>`.
`AVG(salary)` over the whole `employees` table gives the company average.

sql.starter:
SELECT name, salary
FROM employees
-- TODO: keep only employees paid more than the company average
ORDER BY salary DESC, name;
sql.solution:
SELECT name, salary
FROM employees
WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees)
ORDER BY salary DESC, name;
